articleTitle: Observed Characteristics of Lightning Attachment to the Wind Turbines and Its Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: In the present study, we analysed lightning flash strokes attached on the wind turbines. The data was simultaneously measured through a comprehensive lightning observation system in the Zhangbei wind farm in 2017 located in northwest of China. The camera and the related time-synchronized magnetic field are included in the present study. Based on magnetic field data, optical images, and data from the lightning location system, it is shown that the flashes demonstrated a noticeably large number of return strokes for strokes to the wind turbines in Zhangbei wind farm, with an average number of 8. The arithmetic mean and geometric mean of the time interval of all return strokes were 63.38 ms and 45.06 ms, respectively. The distance between the striking point and the observational site ranged from 7 km to 9 km. The current of each return stroke ranged from 3.8 kA to 62.9 kA. The median value of 50% of the current peak is 19.2 kA. The magnetic field waveforms all behave as microsecond-scale fast variations, and the magnetic field waveforms were all similar in shape. The 10-90% risetime ranged from 0.6 μs to 2.2 μs, the arithmetic mean and geometric mean are 1.1 μs and 1.0 μs. The half-peak width ranged from from 1.2 μs to 6.3 μs, the arithmetic mean and geometric mean are 3.4 μs and 3.3 μs, respectively. Furthermore, comparing peak value of magnetic field and lightning current, the magnetic field is approximately linear with the current as expected.

articleTitle: Microgrid formation as a resilient strategy for load restoration and preventing voltage collapse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: In the recent years, the electric power system reinforcement against natural disasters has become one of the key challengers and concerns. The natural disasters, events and cyber-attacks are the most important challenges facing distribution networks causing widespread outages and blackouts. One of the useful techniques to cope with such problems is to utilize the microgrid formation strategy. This paper applies microgrid formation for load restoration and preventing voltage collapse. The given model enhances the system resilience following events. The proposed microgrid formation is developed by utilizing the tie-line breaker switches (BS). The IEEE 33-bus network is considered as case study and both the active-reactive powers are included in the power flow equation. The mixed integer linear planning (MILP) is used and the nonlinear equations are efficiently linearized. The results are presented under three cases including (i) without formation, (ii) formation without tie-lines, and (iii) formation with tie-lines. The numerical results demonstrate that the supplied loads in cases 1 to 3 are 57%, 64% and 71%, respectively. Therefore, the load restoration under cases 2 and 3 is increased by 7% and 14%, respectively. As well, the results illustrate that the proposed model not only improves the voltage profile but also reduces the generated power by DGs resulting in less environmental pollutions and costs.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wind Power Forecasts via Bias Correction Technologies for Numerical Weather Prediction Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This study aims to improve wind power forecasts using the bias correction technologies for NWP wind speeds, which proposed a suitable post processing strategy to correct NWP outputs. In this study, three NWP models (Radar Weather Research and Forecasting (RWRF), Deterministic Weather Research and Forecasting (WRFD), and a 20-member WRF ensemble prediction system (WEPS)) provided by Taiwan Central Weather Bureau (CWB) were systematically bias corrected using decaying average (DA) and probability matching mean (PMM) to improve wind-speed forecasts. With the bias correction of NWP products, this study performed hourly-ahead wind power forecasts using machine learning (Long short-term memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost)) and deep learning (Transformer) models. The results demonstrate that the forecasting accuracy after the bias correction of NWP wind speeds was improved. Compared with the experiments without bias correction, the RMSE for wind speed in RWRF, WRFD and WEPS during the validation months are decreased by 46.13%, 5.84% and 3.82%, respectively, and the accuracy of wind power prediction is improved as well. In this regard, the necessity of NWP correction in a typical forecasting process is verified.

articleTitle: Observed Induced Overvoltage on the Test Overhead Distribution initiated from Natural Lightning Activities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: A new rocket-triggered lightning experiment site has been established by us in Zhanjiang, Guangdong Province, China since the summer of 2022, for the aim of the direct or indirect coupling effect research on industrial systems such as wind turbine, overhead distribution line system, small-scale steel building structure, and buried cables due to both the natural and rocket-triggered lightning flash. This paper reports the lightning-induced overvoltage observed on a test overhead distribution line, caused by 24 natural lightning return-stroke events during 2 consecutive days of afternoon thunderstorms. Comparing with the results of the rocket-triggered LIV reported by Wang et al. and Cai et al., and the natural LIV observations by Yang et al., the general characteristics of the recorded pulse waveforms are similar, while there is a significant difference in the 10%-90% rising time of the first positive wave peak of the LIVs. Considering the recorded much lower amplitude of the waveforms, the phenomenon can be reasonably illustrated by the fact that lightning activity occurs farther away from the observation site and the high-frequency attenuation of EM propagation is more significant. Meanwhile, three LIVs waveforms were recorded to have the initial reverse polarity wave before the return-stroke-induced first positive waves, which are regarded to be leader-process response and are impacted by the location of the lightning relative to the line. The report is an important guide for the research and practice techniques of lightning activity monitoring, localization, and overvoltage surge identification based on the line monitoring devices in real operation.

articleTitle: Seaport Integrated Energy Management: Leveraging Reversible Solid Oxide Cell Energy System for Sustainable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper presents an integrated energy management strategy for seaports, addressing the challenges of localized imbalances resulting from independent management of various energy sources. Leveraging reversible solid oxide cell (ReSOC) technology, capable of bidirectional conversion in both solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) and solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) modes, the proposed approach enhances flexibility in energy systems. To manage the intricacies of the ReSOC model within seaport environments, a novel deep reinforcement learning (DRL) framework is introduced. Through case studies, the paper validates the effectiveness and superior performance of the proposed strategy, offering valuable insights for the practical implementation of ReSOC-based energy management in seaports.

articleTitle: Experimental Study of Open-Switch Faults for Interfacing Inverters in Microgrids Using OPAL-RT Real-time Simulator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: With increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in power distribution systems, the microgrid becomes a fundamental building block for grid modernization. Within a microgrid, renewable energy-based distributed generation (DG) units are connected through interfacing inverters. These inverters play an essential role for the microgrid operation by employing advanced control schemes. However, interfacing inverters may fail due to various faults. In this paper, an experimental investigation of open-switch faults for the DG interfacing voltage source inverter (VSI) in microgrids is conducted using the Opal-RT real-time simulator test bench, where three grid-forming inverter control schemes for DGs (droop control, virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control, and VSG with Fuzzy secondary controller) are implemented under healthy and 21 single- and multi-open-switch fault combinations. In addition to three control schemes, five inverter loadings (30%, 45%, 60%, 75% and 90%) are also considered in the testing. Three phase voltage and current signals recorded at the inverter output/load terminal in these experiments provide unique and novel datasets for studying inverter open-switch fault diagnosis in microgrids.

articleTitle: Analysis of Shunt Reactor Switching at a 115 kV Substation and Its Effects on the Circuit Switcher
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper contains the results of the shunt reactor switching study performed for a 25 MVAR shunt reactor in a 115kV Substation. The objective of this shunt reactor switching study was to determine the worst case transient recovery voltages (TRVs) imposed on the circuit switcher (CS) as well as the transient overvoltages (TOVs) imposed on the 25MVAR shunt reactor. After the simulation results indicated that TRVS may damage the CS, the authors recommended proper TRV mitigation for circuit switcher which also benefited the reactor from TOVs.

articleTitle: Research on Solar Irradiance Distribution and Correlation with Photovoltaic Generated Output: A Case Study of Wuhan and Zhangbei, China
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The development of renewable energy is a crucial strategy for addressing global energy shortages and environmental pollution. Solar energy, noted for its cleanliness and renewability, has become a significant source of renewable energy. Studying the distribution of solar energy resources is essential due to the cyclical, fluctuating, and seasonal nature of solar irradiance. This paper examines the primary factors influencing solar irradiation, utilizing data on solar irradiance and photovoltaic output from Wuhan and Zhangbei, China, in 2022. The findings indicate that solar irradiance in China reaches its minimum during winter and peaks during summer. On sunny days, solar irradiance typically exhibits a single-peak trend, while on cloudy and rainy days, it shows greater volatility. Solar irradiance primarily consists of direct normal irradiance on sunny and partially cloudy days, and diffuse horizontal irradiance on overcast and rainy days. This study could provide a theoretical foundation for positioning photovoltaic power installations and for further predicting solar irradiance and photovoltaic power output in future research.

articleTitle: Resonant Frequency in Renewable Energy Facilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: One of the objectives of the harmonic analysis for utility-scale wind, solar or battery energy storage projects is the calculation of the resonant frequencies at the point of interconnection. Presented in this paper is a simple method for the estimation of the first resonant frequency at the point of interconnection for a renewable energy facility. This method accounts for the capacitance of the filters in converters and inverters, and the capacitance of collector system cables. Also presented in this paper is the general expression for the estimation of the first resonant frequency in facilities with multiple substation transformers. Examples show the case of harmonic analysis results affected by the presence of nearby renewable energy facilities. The analysis also shows the sensitivity of the resonant frequency to equipment rating deviations.

articleTitle: Analysis of non-contact measurement methods for sag of overhead transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Amidst the global integration of renewable energy sources to combat the energy crisis and foster low-carbon power systems, expanding power transmission lines becomes imperative, significantly elevating operational risks. This paper addresses the crucial concern of sag in power lines and explores non-contact measurement methods for sag through advanced magnetoresistive materials, focusing on spatial magnetic field characteristics. Three reference lines—tower longitudinal line, projection line, and center perpendicular line—are investigated through finite element simulations. The results provide valuable insights by suggesting optimal locations for sensor placement, delineating linear correlations between magnetic field intensity and sag values, and presenting a novel sag measurement method by finding the maximum magnetic field strength point in the Z-axis component. These results contribute to efficient and cost-effective sag monitoring in overhead transmission lines, which is crucial for enhancing the safety and reliability of power systems amid renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: A Prototype of Smart Clock and Load Consumption Buzzer: PowerAlert
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Residential housing is increasingly oriented toward all-electric consumption, also replacing gas loads. Users are under contract by an electricity provider that sets a power threshold above which the supplied is interrupted, that means it is increasingly difficult to stay below the threshold. The paper proposes an innovative device, called PowerAlert, that could show real-time power consumption with an audible signal related to the power thresholds set by the user. It is possible to switch the display between power consumption and the real-time clock with a simple push button.During device configuration is possible to connect it to a wireless network, to set a power meter among those available and its IP address. It is also possible to set three power thresholds referred to three different frequencies of the buzzer as alarm. This device can also be useful for monitoring modern electric devices that work in pulse mode and thermally stress protections that might intervene later.

articleTitle: EV Charging Station Implementation in Urban and Non-Urban Areas: Policies, Challenges, and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The rapid demand for electric vehicles (EVs) is increasingly driving the creation of new charging infrastructure for more cars. The year 2023 has seen an unprecedented increase in EVs, also aided by the goal of reducing emissions with clear medium- and short-term targets. This paper proposes an analysis on EV charging station infrastructure in urban and non-urban areas. The policies, challenges and opportunities related to the EV charging stations (EVCSs) will be explored. Also, the integration of EVs with the grid and the new opportunities that are emerging related to charging station will be investigated.

articleTitle: Charging pile fault diagnosis method based on BOA-SSA-BP neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: To address the issue of frequent faults in direct current electric vehicle charging piles and the difficulty of precise diagnosis, presenting an enhanced Back Propagation neural network (BP) as a basis for a fault diagnosis approach in charging equipment. Firstly, the operation data set of the charging pile is preprocessed, such as normalization and filling in missing values, and the preprocessed dataset is fed into the BP model for training purposes. Secondly, an enhanced optimization technique combining the Butterfly Optimization Algorithm(BOA) and the Sparrow Search Algorithm(SSA) is introduced to optimize the weights and thresholds of the BP model, resulting in the acquisition of an optimal model. Finally, the fault status of the charging pile is diagnosed based on the optimized BP model. The simulation results show that the proposed improved BP method has good computational advantages in terms of Mean Absolute Error (MAE), Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE), and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). Compared with the diagnostic accuracy of the traditional BP algorithm, the improved BP method increased by 14.85%, which can diagnose the state of the charging pile accurately, providing a strong guarantee for the fault diagnosis of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Coupling Performance of Secondary Cables in Substation with Different Terminal Load and Surge Injection Position
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: During lightning strike on a power substation grounding facility, surge currents flow into the substation's grounding system, where inducing coupling effects in the secondary cables happens. There is currently limited research on the influence of cable terminal load and grounding-grid dispersion paths on the induced coupling of secondary cables. In this paper, the effects of four terminal load modes and two grounding grid dispersion methods on cable port voltage are investigated using both time-domain and frequency-domain methods. The results show that the core induced voltage amplitude is highest when the cable is grounded only at the far end through the load, reaching twice as much as when the cable is grounded at both end. The dispersion of ground grid current pathway significantly impacts cable-induced voltages in both time and frequency domain, particularly in scenarios involving near-ended grounding by load and double-ended ungrounding. Following the transition of the grounding grid dispersal method from the right side to the central extended grounding body injection, there is an overall reduction of approximately 10-30% in the f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3dB</inf>. Buried cables are more susceptible to variations in the dispersion path of the grounding grid compared to ground cables.

articleTitle: Learning Assisted Resilient Load Restoration with Distributed Mobile Resources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Extreme natural disasters are characterized by high impact and low probability, which can cause significant damage to power systems. Distributed Mobile Resources (DMRs), including mobile energy storage systems (MESSs), heavy-duty electric trucks, and private electric vehicles (EVs), can enhance the resilience of power systems in the face of such disasters through their flexible charging and discharging capabilities. In this paper, we introduce a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based method for efficiently dispatching DMRs to achieve the rapid restoration of critical loads in the event of disasters, thereby enhancing the resilience of the power grid. Firstly, this paper creates a detailed physical hurricane model and calculates equivalent wind speeds for distinct segments of distribution lines at various intervals, estimating the likelihood of line damage. DMRs, which are treated as agents in our approach, formulate real-time strategies for routing and discharging, informed by damage assessments and their current operational state. Our model-free algorithm enhances the accuracy in characterizing disaster scenarios and expedites the formulation of optimal scheduling strategies. Simulation studies demonstrate that DMRs can collaborate effectively, substantially enhancing the system’s resilience in disaster situations.

articleTitle: Study on the health status of lithium-ion batteries based on relaxation voltage characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Over-discharge of lithium-ion batteries can seriously affect the performance and service life of lithium batteries. In order to characterize the aging degree of Li-ion batteries under the consideration of over-discharge, this paper proposes a method for extracting the health status factor of Li-ion batteries based on the voltage drop characteristics during the relaxation period. Firstly, the experimental platform of Li-ion battery over-discharge is set up to obtain the data of Li-ion battery over-discharge; Secondly, the induction mechanism of Li-ion battery internal short-circuit induced by over-discharge is theoretically analyzed; Lastly, the characteristic quantity of voltage drop during the relaxation period of the Li-ion battery is extracted after it is fully charged to obtain the characterization of the battery health status factor, and the degree of aging is classified through the method of clustering. The results show that the proposed battery health status factor can better characterize the aging degree of lithium battery.

articleTitle: Soft start optimization using NTC resistors in fault managed power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Inrush current limiting methods using Negative Temperature Coefficient (NTC) resistors in power converter circuits are prominent choices in device and system protection schemes. In this paper, a newly developed equipment protection algorithm is introduced, which involves the temporary inclusion of NTC resistors in fault-managed power circuits. The circuit configuration is robust and highly energy-efficient as it maximizes startup capabilities, using the NTC resistor’s self-heat feature to soft start larger loads by fully utilizing the NTC resistor’s energy capacity while still being efficient by bypassing the NTC resistor afterwards. The control algorithm is developed and applied in a real-world Packet Energy Transfer (PET) system. Simulation models were validated with experimental results for a performance study of the soft start circuit.

articleTitle: Novel Frequency Control Technologies for Wind Turbines Based on Modified Gaussian Curve Settings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper concentrates on the frequency control technologies by WTs. Especially, stepwise inertia control (SIC)– related controls were discussed, and a modified Gaussian power curve- based control has been developed. The inspiration of this control method from Gaussian curves, which adjusts the shape characteristics of the Gaussian curve by tuning the associated parameters to achieve frequency regulation by WTs. When a frequency event occurs, WTs support an additional power immediately and then follow a reference power output based on the modified Gaussian curve equation. This study employed the user-defined model functionality of PSS/E, and an actual Taiwan Power Company (Taipower) system was used to verify the feasibility of the proposed control methods for WTs.

articleTitle: Large-Signal Stability Analysis of DC Microgrid System Considering the Power Characterization of Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The negative impedance characterizaiton of constant power loads (CPLs) easily causes instability of direct current (DC) microgrid systems. Energy storage systems play an important role in the stability of DC microgrid systems. A large-signal stability analysis process that considers power characterization of energy storage system is presented in this paper. Firstly, an equal model of DC microgrid system is derived. The power characterization of energy storage system is analysed based on previous work. Then, the Lyapunov-based stability analysis and existence of equilibrium points are discussed. Two muti-constraints stability criterias are proposed. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of proposed method.

articleTitle: Communication Assisted Permissive Underreach Transfer Tripping Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: In this paper, the robust features of wireless sensor networks are utilized in tele-protection systems. Cognitive radio algorithms are applied to transfer tripping signals from one substation to another in a permissive underreach transfer tripping scheme. The dependability, security, and cost of the proposed scheme is discussed within this paper and is compared with other common communication links in tele-protection schemes. The proposed scheme offers a broad communication network that allows the relays at the remote substations to communicate with each other which permits a more dependable backup protection without the need for third zone settings of the distance relay. Hence, the impacts of load encroachment and infeed are mitigated. A cyber-physical co-simulation is run in MATLAB/SIMULINK<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> to investigate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Study on the Strategies to Mitigate the Effects of Partial Shading on PV Power Generation Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The main purpose of this paper is to explore various possible strategies to reduce the impacts of partial shading on the output of the PV systems. First, under various typical partial shading scenarios, the topology of various PV modules and the connections of bypass diodes were evaluated to determine the best structure for them. Next, this paper compared different maximum power tracking control strategies, and combined with the reconfiguration strategies. It aims to improve the overall power generation performance in a shading environment. Finally, this paper studied the impact of different voltage converter configurations on the shading effect, and then proposed the optimal voltage converter configuration. These converters include central, single string or micro configurations. Through simulations, a complete strategy for reducing the impact of shading was proposed for solar photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Energy-Aware Data Center Job Scheduling Scheme under Uncertain Environment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: As a pivotal industrial infrastructure in the digital age, data centers are facing rapidly increasing energy consumption and costs. Leveraging the operational nature of data centers, job scheduling can be employed to adjust job execution times, providing temporal flexibility in energy consumption. However, the inherent uncertainties associated with job arrivals and electricity prices pose significant challenges to effective job scheduling. In this paper, we propose a data center job scheduling scheme based on distributional reinforcement learning to capture the uncertainty of job arrivals and prices for a better operation strategy. Firstly, we formulate the job scheduling problem within the Markov decision process framework. To solve the problem of uncertainty faced by the data center, we introduce a scheduling model based on Quantile Regression Deep Q-Network. Finally, the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can adaptively optimize the data center job scheduling strategy.

articleTitle: Apply K-means Cluster Analysis to Perform Adaptive Protection IED in Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: A microgrid consists of distributed energy resources (DERs) and loads. Due to the intermittent power generation of DERs and the changeable operation mode of microgrid, the magnitude and direction of fault currents are not fixed once a fault occurs in the microgrid. The protection scheme based on the traditional radial distribution system can no longer meet the protection requirements of microgrid. This study develops a microgrid protection management system (PMS) that follows the IEC 61850 protocol and integrates intelligent electronic devices (IEDs) and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) platforms. Through the IED logic configuration and GOOSE mechanism, the circuit breaker tripping and blocking signals can be transmitted between IEDs to achieve protection of microgrid line, busbar and back-up protection. To solve the limitation of the number of IED setting group, this paper uses cluster analysis to group the microgrid operation status. The results can be used as the basis for IEDs setting groups. Based on the microgrid operation information collected by SCADA, the PMS can determine the setting groups of IEDs. The results show that the PMS can select the appropriate setting groups of IEDs under different microgrid operation situations to achieve the purpose of microgrid fault protection.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Approaches for the Differential Protection of Power Transformers Using Advanced Classification Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The transformer is one of the costlier and critical assets in the power system. Its protection against internal fault is achieved by implementing a differential protection scheme. However, this scheme holds the false tripping risk subjected to high inrush current drawn during transformer energisation. In the proposed work, wavelet transform and artificial intelligence (AI)/machine learning (ML) based schemes are utilised to differentiate internal fault, normal and inrush current signals. The current signals are generated from the MATLAB simulation software. Later, discrete wavelet transform (DWT) is used to extract essential features from the corresponding current signals. In DWT, the mother wavelet and decomposition levels are selected as Daubechies (Db) and level 4 respectively. The extracted features are then fed to various AI/ML models such as k-nearest neighbors, support vector machine, and a multi-layered feed-forward neural network (MLFFNN) trained by the back propagation and resilient back propagation algorithms respectively. The results of these models are then compared to examine the accuracy of the model at utility/industry-defined sampling frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fault Potential Assessment under Typical Line-fault in a Real Urban Old Community
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Electric shock is always an issue of concern in residential power system, especially in an old residential community with increasing electrical loads. The past literature usually reports calculated results based on a typical low-voltage distribution line system with a single building. In this study, the fault potential in multiple buildings of a real old residential community under specific phase-to-ground fault is investigated using the partial element equivalent circuit (PEEC) model with the buried conductors and overhead line systems, the actual wiring, grounding configurations, and protective earthing methods considered in the simulation. The main LV switch box, main distribution box, overhead lines, and each building are of concern in the assessment as both fault positions and observation positions. It is found that when a phase-to-ground fault occurs outside the residential buildings, e.g., sub-main distribution box, the fault potential could be easily transferred into most of the buildings with a PE wire connected with the N wire. The effective value would be more significant than 24V, a generally guided safe threshold value for human-body electric shock. For the line fault cases that occur in the buildings, the fault potential distribution and the threat to the other measured positions mainly depend on the protective earthing method, while the line topology outside the building has little effect on the fault potential distribution. Three typical grounding methods existing in the concerned urban villages are all discussed and compared in the study.

articleTitle: Second Harmonic-Based Approach to Identify a GIC Flow in Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Certain parts of the world can experience active geomagnetic disturbances, which trigger geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) to flow through grounding circuits into power systems. Such currents are quasi-dc currents that can have large magnitudes capable of inflecting damage to power system equipment. Power transformers are among the vulnerable equipment to GIC flows, which can cause harmonic distortion, disruption in reactive power flow, and thermal damage in transformer windings. Adverse effects of GIC flows can be minimized by developing a fast, accurate, and reliable detection method of GICs. Such a detection method can support initiating adequate responses to block the GIC from flowing into power transformers. This paper presents the development and implementation of a method to detect GIC flows in power transformers. The developed method is based on extracting the second harmonic present in the differential currents. The proposed GIC detection is experimentally tested using laboratory 3φ transformers, when operated for different GIC flows and loading levels. In addition, experimental tests are conducted for magnetizing inrush currents and various faults in both sides of tested transformers. Test results demonstrate fast and accurate detection of GIC flows with minor sensitivity to the value of the GIC, loading level, and/or transformer core type. In addition, the proposed 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonicbased method is found able to accurately distinguish GIC flows from magnetizing inrush and fault currents.

articleTitle: Detecting Arcing Current Faults in Medium-to-Low Voltage Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Arcing current faults occurring in a medium-to-low voltage (MV-LV) transformer can pose a challenge for transformer protection. Such faults trigger currents with lower magnitudes than those triggered by conventional faults, thus making it difficult for transformer protection to accurately detect and respond to arcing current faults. This paper proposes a method for accurate detection and identification of arcing current faults in MV-LV transformers. The presented method is based on extracting the magnitudes and phases of low frequency harmonics from the differential currents. Unlike magnetizing inrush and conventional fault currents, arcing current faults trigger currents that have harmonic components with non-stationary phases. These non-stationary phases can provide signature information of arcing current faults. Non-stationary phases can be extracted using a multi-channel filter bank that is composed of digital bandpass finite impulse response filters, each of which has a linear phase over a wide frequency range. The non-stationary phase method is tested during various fault and non-fault events. Test results demonstrate accurate and reliable detection, identification, and response to arcing current faults with minor sensitivity to loading level and/or arcing current fault type (series or parallel).

articleTitle: Harmonic Distortions in 3ϕ Auto-Transformers Due to Geomagnetically Induced Currents
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Geomagnetic disturbances can trigger large geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) to flow into power systems through grounded equipment. Several studies identify power transformers (with grounded windings) as the main path for GIC flows into power systems. The flow of a GIC (dominated by a dc component) through grounded windings of a power transformer can lead to severe impacts on its functionality, such as significant increases in its reactive power demands, high levels of current harmonic distortions, and possible thermal damages. This article presents case studies and analyses of harmonic distortions in 3ϕ power auto-transformers during GIC flows. Case studies and analyses are conducted using data collected from laboratory experiments. Analyzed data sets are collected from 3ϕ power auto-transformers with different power ratings, voltages ratings, and core types. Furthermore, analyzed sets of data are collected for various levels of GIC flows. Analysis results reveal that the dc component and 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic dominate the 3ϕ currents in grounded windings of tested 3ϕ power auto-transformers over a wide range of GIC flows. In addition, the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup>, 4<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 6<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, 7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup>, and 8<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> harmonic components are present with low magnitudes.

articleTitle: One-Node Method to Implement Smart Grid Functions Using a Battery Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper develops and tests the performance of the one-node method for implementing aggregated smart grid functions to operate residential loads. The developed method is based on utilizing a battery storage system (BSS) at the point-of-supply feeding the target residential loads. The power ratings of the BSS can be selected based on the required reduction in the load power demands during the peak-demand hours. Furthermore, the charging and discharging of the BSS are set based on peak-demand and off-peak demand hours and stability constraints for voltage and frequency at the point-of-supply. The proposed operation of the BSS is set to have it charge energy during off-peak-demand hours, and discharge energy during peak-demand hours. The energy charge into the BSS can be viewed as the equivalent thermal energy storage in thermostatically controlled appliances (TCAs), when operated using smart grid functions. The one-node with a BSS method is implemented and tested for a university campus that has 45 buildings, which are fed from one substation (point-of-supply) through a distribution system. Tests are conducted for the Summer and Winter seasons to demonstrate the efficacy of the developed method. Test results demonstrate accurate adjustments of power demands during peak-demand and off-peak-demand hours, along with simple structure to operate the BSS. Moreover, test results show the ability of the one-node method to reduce power losses and improve the voltage at the point-of-supply during peak-demand hours.

articleTitle: Impedance Grounding for Variable-Frequency Electric Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The grounding system for a variable-frequency electric motor drive (VFD) is typically designed to enhance the continuity of operation, limit ground fault currents, limit transient over-voltages during ground faults, improve safety, and reduce or eliminate common-mode voltages (CMVs). The majority of VFDs utilize power transformers to provide isolation between the VFD and its supply, and operate as the point-of-supply to the front-ac-dc power electronic converter (PEC). Grounding system designs for VFDs have been a subject of several standards, industrial codes, and recommended practices. This paper analyzes the performance of impedance grounding systems (during steady-state and fault conditions), when utilized in VFDs. Analyzed grounding systems are the low-resistance, and high-resistance grounding systems. The performance of analyzed grounding systems is evaluated based ground currents, ground potential, and CMVs. Several experimental tests are also conducted to draw conclusions and suggest recommendations for an adequate impedance grounding for industrial VFDs.

articleTitle: Effects of Grounding Impedance on the Second Harmonic Component Produced by GIC Flows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Geomagnetic disturbances trigger quasi-dc currents that flow through grounding circuits into power systems, mostly through power transformers. Geomagnetically-induced currents (GICs) can cause severe harmonic distortions, disruption in reactive power flow, and/or thermal damage to power transformers. These adverse effects of GIC flows on power transformers depend on the GIC magnitude, transformer core design, grounding circuit, and winding configuration. This paper analyzes the effects of grounding circuit designs on the adverse impacts of GIC flows in power transformers. These effects are analyzed through experimental tests carried out using laboratory 3ϕ, multi-core power transformers. Experimental tests are performed for several grounding circuit designs for the test power transformers. Normal, magnetizing inrush, line-to-line, and line-to-neutral fault conditions are conducted for each tested grounding circuit design. Results of experimental tests show that grounding circuits with low impedance have minor effects on the GIC flows, while grounding circuits with high impedance tend to reduce the magnitude of the GIC. In addition, test results demonstrate that grounding circuits have little influence on the harmonic distortion (mainly the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> harmonic component) created by a GIC flow.

articleTitle: Impacts of Loading Level on Harmonic Distortion in 3ϕ Auto-Transformers During GIC Flows
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Geomagnetically induced currents (GICs) are quasi-dc currents that flow through grounding circuits into power systems. These currents are triggered by geomagnetic disturbance events, and flow into power systems through grounded, power system components, including 3ϕ auto-transformers. A GIC flow through a 3ϕ auto-transformer can lead to high levels of harmonic distortion in currents, overheating of auto-transformer windings, and significant increase in auto-transformer reactive power demands. The severity of GIC flow impacts on a 3ϕ auto-transformer can be dependent on the core design, winding configuration, grounding circuit, and GIC current. This paper discusses possible contributions of loading levels to GIC impacts on a 3ϕ auto-transformer. These possible contributions are analyzed through experimental tests carried out using a laboratory 3ϕ, multi-core auto-transformer. Experimental tests are conducted for various GIC flows, where the loading level is varied. Test results conclude that the loading level of a 3ϕ auto-transformer can influence the harmonic distortion created by a GIC flow. In addition, test results show that loading level and load power factor have influences on the reactive power demands of a 3ϕ auto-transformer, when experiencing a GIC flow.

articleTitle: One-Node Approach to Implement Smart Grid Functions without Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper presents and tests a one-node method for implementing smart grid functions to operate residential loads. The proposed method is developed based on adjusting the power demands of residential loads to achieve a desired load-demand profile at the supply node. A desired load-demand profile is set based on operating thermostatically controlled appliances (TCAs) in the target residential loads. Smart grid functions are implemented to operate TCAs so that thermal energy is stored during the daily off-peak-demand hours. This stored thermal energy is discharged during daily peak-demand hours in order to reduce power demands of residential loads during these hours. The command power assigned to each TCA controller (set to implement smart grid functions) is initiated using a modified-profile for residential load hosting these TCAs. The one-node method is implemented and tested for a university campus that has 45 buildings. Each building has central central heating units and water heaters, and some buildings have central air conditioner units. Tests are performed for different seasons, where power demands of campus buildings are controlled by peak-demand management (as a smart grid function). Test results show the accuracy and simplicity of the one-node method to assign command values for each building to ensure reduced power losses and improved voltage.

articleTitle: Fault Type and Location Identifications of the Hybrid Utility Power and Renewable-Energy-Based Multi-Generation Systems using Nonintrusive Monitoring Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: In the face of hybrid utility power and renewable-energy-based multi-generation systems, if the traditional monitoring system, i.e., the high-speed global positioning system (GPS) combined with the phasor measurement unit (PMU), is adopted, PMUs and protection relays are installed at one or both ends of each transmission line and the internal sides of the renewable-energy-based multi-generation systems. These devices not only increase the complexity of data collection but also increase the cost of system construction. Generally, the monitoring system of renewable-energy generation systems mainly focuses on steady-state demand responses. Since the accuracy of steady-state faulty signatures is low and the calculation of fault data acquisition takes a long time, the analysis of internal and external faults of the systems is extended in response time and is difficult to identify. This paper proposes nonintrusive monitoring techniques, such as installing current sensors at the import power entry points to identify the fault types and locations. The results reveal that the proposed methods demonstrate high success rates of more than 96.2162% and 72.7564% for fault type and location identifications, respectively.

Author Keywords: Hybrid utility power and renewable-energy-based multi-generation systems

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Industrial Motor-Driven Systems and Standards Toward Net Zero Carbon
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Promoting energy-efficient technologies stands out as a highly cost-effective strategy for diminishing global energy demand and greenhouse gas emissions. This contribution significantly aids global endeavors to mitigate climate change. Given that electric motor systems account for more than 50% of overall electricity consumption, substantial potential savings are associated with adopting energy-efficient motor-driven system technologies in new installations and replacing old inefficient motor systems in existing applications. Despite the robustness of industrial electric motors, with a potential service lifetime of over 20 years, the current global motor stock remains inefficient despite international policy initiatives, including minimum efficiency standards. This paper provides an overview of the next generation of industrial motor-driven system technologies, including the best commercially available AC motors, silicon-carbide variable-speed motor drives, regenerative drives, and digitalization. The paper also assesses the current installed base of electric motors, suggests potential policy measures to enhance industrial motor system efficiency, and estimates the energy savings associated with the widespread adoption of high-efficiency motors and motor-driven systems, which, at the World level, may reach 1000 TWh/year.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term Power Probabilistic Forecasting Method for Distributed Photovoltaic based on Joint Distribution Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Accurate probabilistic forecasting of distributed photovoltaic (DPV) ultra-short-term power can provide comprehensive information for power system scheduling and is of great significance for the operation of distribution networks. Addressing the issue of limited consideration of the dependency between photovoltaic power forecasting results and forecast errors in existing research, this paper proposes a DPV ultra-short-term power probabilistic forecasting method based on joint distribution modeling. This method effectively enhances the accuracy of probabilistic forecasting. Firstly, deterministic point forecasting of ultra-short-term power are obtained using an LSTM neural network, resulting in single-point forecasting results and forecasting errors. Then, based on these point forecasting results and errors, Copula function is used to fit the cumulative probability distribution of the point forecasting and errors, thereby constructing a joint probability distribution. Subsequently, based on the desired confidence level, upper and lower bounds of the forecasting errors corresponding to the point forecasting are obtained and added to the point forecasting, enabling the achievement of DPV ultra-short-term probabilistic forecasting. Finally, the superiority of the proposed method is validated through experiments with real-world datasets.

articleTitle: Practical Approaches to Perform Transient Stability Studies for Industrial and Commercial Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Many industrial and commercial power systems have installed generation facilities on-site for the purpose of increasing efficiency, reducing electricity cost, and improving system reliability and resiliency. Adding synchronous generators to local power systems brings stability concerns and tremendously increases complexity in system planning and operation. By principle of power system operation, all running synchronous machines interconnected in the same electrical network are required to remain in synchronism with each other; otherwise they will become unstable and eventually lose the rotor angle stability, which can be quickly propagated across the entire network to cause a system-wide shut down. Following IEEE standards and industrial practices, and leveraging authors’ extensive experience in modeling power system dynamics and conducting transient stability studies, this paper addresses approaches and procedures to perform transient stability study step-by-step in aiming to help power engineers to understand fundamentals and knowledge sets required in this technical space. The paper also introduces basic transient stability study scenario considerations and protection methods to ensure instability issues are identified and stable system operations are verified. The most recent relevant IEEE standards, IEEE task force reports and industrial literatures on transient stability study are referenced in the paper.

articleTitle: Vehicle-to-Home Service Via Electric Vehicle Energy Storage Virtual Partitioning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The need of a change in many energy paradigm in view of a sustainable energy transition is introducing novel challenges in many fields such as power production, transmission, distribution and utilization. Also on the user side, defining new strategies to reach energy neutrality and sustainability is an important step in this process. This paper proposes a Virtual Partitioning Algorithm (VPA) for Electric Vehicles (EVs) energy storage system to provide vehicles-to-home (V2H) services in an novel and effective manner. The VPA will allow improving the environmental and economic performance of prosumers with residential photovoltaic systems without the need of installing dedicated flexibility devices, e.g. battery energy storage systems, or in co-operation with existing storage units if present. The VPA for V2H services is applied to a realistic residential test-case using real measured data and results highlighted its positive performances both from a economic and energy independence point of view.

articleTitle: Renewable Energy Communities Virtual Islanding: A Novel Service for Smart Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The needs to actuate a sustainable energy transition is pushing the electricity system and its operators to define new strategies and solutions to make the energy system more flexible and resilient, and to include a bigger share of renewable energy sources. This paper proposes a novel flexibilization service for the distribution system exploiting the capabilities of Renewable Energy Communities through the concept of Virtual Islanding operation. This new paradigm can ease the sustainable energy transition of distribution system, making them keener to accommodate larger shares of renewable sources in the grid. The concept of Virtual Islanding is described in the paper and a methodology to assess its benefits in electricity distribution networks is proposed. The effectiveness of Renewable Energy Communities Virtual Islanding operation is assessed in a simplified distribution system layout with massive penetration of RES, highlighting the benefits both from a technical and sustainability viewpoint.

articleTitle: Long-term Clustered Unit Commitment Considering Lack-of-Inertia and Lack-of-Flexiramp Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Long-term unit commitment (LT-UC) is the essential tool for operators to estimate the feasibilities of weekly/seasonal electrical production and operation processes. With the increase of renewable resources integrating into the power system, finding a suitable schedule commitment through LT-UC for maintaining adequate ramping reserve and frequency reserve against dynamic net-load fluctuations in low inertia gird becomes challenging. To solve this problem, this paper designs a refined LT-UC model to cope with multi-period requirements, including lack-of-inertia capabilities and lack-of-flexiramp ones, resulting from various net-load variabilities and uncertainties. In particular, a recognition method concerning lack-of-inertia and lack-of-flexiramp event screening is designed; then, associated security constraints concerning lack-of-inertia and lack-of-flexiramp connected to relevant intervals are extended. An improved LT-UC model is carried out by incorporating these derived constraints into LT-UC. Furthermore, to accelerate the computational time of the proposed model, a concise clustered LT-UC model that treats homogenization units into a clustered unit is re-constructed. Results are conducted based on a modified version of the IEEE 6-bus test system and the IEEE 30-bus test system, and the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed model are tested by comparing it with existing empirical models.

articleTitle: A Proposed Guide for the Energy Plan and Electrical Infrastructure of a Port
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: A guideline for the port system master plan must provide innovative and redevelopment solutions in short, medium and long-term energy planning. It can contribute in the competitiveness competition of its geographical sector to the pursuit of objectives of high performance, functionality, service continuity (Business Continuity) and eco-sustainability. The provision of organizational procedures and tools can favor the use of the various incentives available or to be promoted with adequate regulation. The use of electricity in the port system area in its overall energy needs and competitive functionality must be managed in a single integrated user vision such as a "port-grid" or port microgrid. The energy and environmental planning of the port system must define the strategic guidelines and specific implementation measures to improve energy efficiency and encourage the use of renewable energy in the port area. In fact, the energy and environmental sustainability criteria must be aimed at satisfying the promoted policies regarding the conversion of all port equipment to zero emissions within the next decade, starting with equipment for handling goods. They require business continuity management for better operational efficiency and a reorganization of the electrical distribution architecture (architecture efficiency) for the unification of all users and the implementation of innovations.

articleTitle: A New Modified Down-sampling DFT based Phasor Estimation Techinque for Power System Protective Relays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Decaying DC offset poses a significant challenge in power systems, especially during fault occurrences. Short circuits generate this Decaying DC offset (DDC) in fault current waveforms. The presence of DDC offset in protection and control systems can lead to system failures or incorrect operations. Phasor estimation techniques based on Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) encounter difficulties in accurately and promptly extracting fundamental characteristics from fault signals due to decaying DC components (DDCs). This complicates the reliable and swift extraction of essential information by protective relays during fault situations. This paper proposes a modification down-sampling algorithm based on DFT, which is derived from the Multiple Delayed Signal Cancellation (MDSC) to estimate the fundamental phasor current signal in a faulted high power transmission line containing one or more Decaying DC (DDC) components such as a primary DDC or secondary DDC caused by the current transformer. Given the improvement in the accuracy of phasor measurement and the elimination of multiple DDCs, a full cycle and an even sample set combination of DFTs is proposed. The DDC error can be obtained by subtracting the full cycle DFT from the even sample set DFT. This method is immune to multiple DDCs. Numerical and simulation tests are implemented to validate the proposed technique, and its performance is compared with four related phasor estimation methods. In the presence of DDCs with the hindrance of noise and harmonics, the proposed method performs well, and the test results show that it can attain fast and accurate phasor estimation. This method is even suitable for eliminating the secondary DDC caused by the current transformer.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Transmission Line Structures Corrosion due to DC Current from Pipeline’s Cathodic Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper investigates corrosion of high-voltage transmission line structures resulting from direct current (DC) emitted by a nearby pipeline’s cathodic protection system. With increasing coexistence of power lines and metallic structures, such as pipelines, in shared corridors, stray current interactions induce electrolytic and electrochemical corrosion in transmission line structures. In this paper, advanced numerical modeling is conducted to analyze such corrosion utilizing the Boundary Element Method (BEM) and a direct solution of Maxwell's equations through COMSOL and CDEGS software, respectively. Two case studies using the developed COMSOL and CDEGS models are conducted by comparing simulation results with field measurements, highlighting the effectiveness of numerical methodologies in analyzing stray current corrosion. Findings in this paper contribute to the development of corrosion protection and mitigation techniques to enhance reliability and durability of power transmission systems.

articleTitle: A Review of the GIC Blocker Placement Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Space weather poses a tremendous threat to power systems: geomagnetic disturbances could result in widespread disruptions and long-duration blackouts, including severe damage to system components. To mitigate their impacts, a handful of strategies exist, with the most promising being the deployment of transformer neutral blocking devices. The high cost of these devices, however, precludes their installation at all substations; this motivates the development of effective solutions for the cost-effective placement of such devices. While the current state-of-the-art in blocker placement methods is insufficient to be applied to real-sized power grids, ongoing research continues to increase the size of networks for which the placement problem remains tractable. Along these lines, the contributions of this paper are two fold: first, a comprehensive overview of the current state-of-the-art in blocker placement methods is provided; and second, a complete optimization formulation – implemented and benchmarked in an open-source software – for the blocker placement problem is presented.

articleTitle: A Review of MVDC Smart Grids Technologies and Components
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The Medium Voltage DC (MVDC) distribution systems represent an innovative solution to fulfill the rapid growth of the energy demand and enabling the integration of an increasingly amount of Distributed Energy resources (DERs) and Energy Storage Systems (ESS) in the electric power system. The high-power supply capability of these systems, as well as the great flexibility and controllability, make them potentially capable of facing up some issues affecting the normal operation of the current AC distribution network. This paper aims to provide a review of MVDC grids, with the specific purpose to show both potential and weakness of these systems. DC rating voltage levels, grid architectures, main components and technologies required for development of these systems are analyzed. The protection of MVDC grids under DC fault conditions is also investigated, in order to outline any form of improvement.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Basic Insulation Level (BIL) Requirements for Distribution-Supplied 38kV Enclosed Switchgear
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: There is a long-standing practice of specification of 200kV BIL on 38kV enclosed switchgear applied at the front-end of 38kV utility substations. By extension, this practice has also proliferated for consumer-owned 38kV switchgear supplied from 38kV utility distribution feeders. This practice has its roots in the desire for utilities to avoid the installation of surge arrestors in this type of switchgear due to maintenance costs and other concerns. However, for switchgear applied as consumer-owned switchgear supplied from utility distribution feeders, it is very common to apply surge arrestors in the switchgear. The insulation coordination and surge arrester parameters of the 38kV enclosed switchgear have been studied. The PSCAD/EMTDC model has been developed for the simulation of lightning overvoltage. This paper evaluates the BIL requirements for consumer-owned switchgear fed from common configurations of 38kV utility distribution lines with and without surge arrestors applied in the switchgear. It also evaluates the need to apply surge arrestors in locations such as bus tie circuit breakers for switchgear fed from multiple distribution lines to achieve suitability of 38kV switchgear with BIL levels that are less than 200kV.

articleTitle: Offshore Wind-Powered Seaport DC Microgrids with EV Stations Using Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The surge in the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) has intensified the demand for a sustainable and reliable charging infrastructure. This study integrates Taiwan's abundant offshore wind energy resources to cater to this demand, particularly in geographically isolated coastal regions. Central to our study is the challenge of managing the power flow complexities introduced by the variability of wind energy coupled with unpredictable EV charging demand. Our innovative approach harnesses the potential of a wind-powered Electric Vehicle Charging System (EVCS) using a medium-voltage direct-current (MVDC) bus. An advanced Model Predictive Control (MPC) strategy was developed to present a decentralized control system. Unlike traditional control systems, this mechanism exhibits enhanced adaptability and efficiently manages the dynamic interplay between wind energy generation, Energy Storage Systems (ESS), EV charging demand, and grid interactions. Our simulations indicate that the MPC maintains voltage stability in the MVDC bus and shows optimal power flow, minimizing energy losses and ensuring grid stability. Although the outcomes presented in this study underscore the viability of the proposed wind-powered EVCS integrated with the grid, extensive real-world evaluations are required to solidify its applicability and scalability in diverse environments.

articleTitle: Research Review on the Energy Coordination and Carbon Evaluation for Agricultural and Animal Husbandry Zero-carbon Parks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Large-scale distributed energy resources integration has brought serious challenges for regional power grid operations such as power redundancy and limited external transmission, there is an urgent need to explore flexible resources to participate in grid safety regulation. Agriculture and animal husbandry have a large amount of controllable power resources and natural negative carbon attributes. On this basis, by integrating comprehensive measures such as improving agricultural and production energy efficiency and generating electricity from biomass waste can achieve self-sustaining carbon cycling and friendly interaction between the park and the power grid. In this paper, based on in-depth analysis of coupling characteristics of energy flows and carbon flows, a flexible load model considering the growth characteristics of plants and animals is established, and a carbon evaluation method considering the biological cycle derivatives is fully explored, thereby modeling a virtual carbon reserve database of the power grid; then, based on different solutions such as heuristic, data-driven methods, the applicable scenarios of various algorithms were analyzed, thereby proposing an energy coordination framework based on game theory to achieve reduce emissions. Finally, future research directions are discussed regarding zero-carbon park management.

articleTitle: Suppression of Subsynchronous Resonance in a Hybrid Steam-Turbine Generator/Offshore Wind Farm System Using a Static Synchronous Compensator with a Vanadium Redox Flow Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: A static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) joined with a vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB)-based energy storage system (ESS) is proposed to suppress subsynchronous resonance (SSR) occurring in a hybrid steam-turbine generator (STG)/offshore wind farm (OWF) system fed to an infinite bus through a series-capacitor compensated line. The OWF is based on a doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) and the d-q axis equivalent-circuit model of the studied system under three-phase balanced loading conditions is derived to establish the complete system. A supplementary damping controller (SDC) of the STATCOM is designed by using modal control theory to improve the damping of the dominant modes of the studied system. Small-signal stability and transient simulation results of the studied system are systematically performed to demonstrate that the proposed STATCOM with the designed SDC combined with the VRFB-ESS is effective in suppressing SSR of the studied system.

articleTitle: A Regional Short-term Load Forecasting Method Based on Adaptive Graph Construction and Kernel Size Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Accurate Short-Term Load Forecasting is very important for power system operation. However, the existing methods for regional load forecasting often lack consideration of the differentiated load characteristics and the interrelationships between various types of loads. Particularly during extreme weather events, demand responses, and other special occurrences, focusing only on the overall trend of regional load changes can lead to significant forecasting errors. Additionally, under extreme weather conditions, various loads within a region exhibit different response patterns. This paper proposes a multivariate time series forecasting model based on an Adaptive Graph Neural Network (ADAGNN) to treat various load types as nodes in a graph network, adaptively constructing adjacency matrices through a graph construction layer to extract inter-load relational information; it also uses graph convolution and temporal convolution to capture different load change patterns in regional loads. Considering the existence of different scales of cyclical changes in time series, an initial dilated convolution method is proposed, endowing the ADAGNN model with the ability to adaptively select the size of convolution kernels to extract multi-scale features of the original series. Ultimately, the model outputs the forecast data for all categorized loads, and the regional load forecast is obtained by summation. A case study is conducted using regional load data from a province in China. Relative to the optimal model in the control group, the proposed ADAGNN model improved by 1.06%, 43.32%, and 42.24% in the MAPE, MAE, and RMSE metrics, respectively, thus validating its high predictive accuracy and scalability.

articleTitle: Stability Improvement of a Multi-Machine Power System Using a DC Microgrid with a Vanadium Redox Flow Battery-based Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper presents the stability-improvement results of a multimachine power system (MMPS) connected with a DC microgrid (MG) consisting of a high-capacity hybrid wind/PV farm, a DC load, and a vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB)-based energy storage system (ESS) with a bidirectional DC/DC converter. The common DC link of the DC MG is integrated into the AC bus of the MMPS through a DC/three-phase AC voltage-source inverter (VSI), a step-up transformer, and a power transmission line. The supplementary damping controllers (SDCs) located at the control loop of the bidirectional DC/DC converter of the VRFB-ESS and the DC/three-phase AC VSI are respectively designed using a pole-placement method based on modal control theory. The simulation results show that the designed SDC at the control loop of the DC/three-phase AC VSI can contribute better damping characteristics to the electromechanical modes of the studied MMPS.

articleTitle: Frequency Synchronization in Isolated AC Micro-Grids by Cooperative Distributed Q-Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: we introduce a novel approach, called cooperative distributed Q-learning, building upon our prior distributed Q-learning methods, aimed at achieving autonomous frequency synchronization within an isolated AC microgrid (MG). Within the framework of multi-agent reinforcement learning, each agent’s objective is to collaboratively determine an optimal policy aligned with the central performance function by exchanging local learning parameters across a communication network. To realize this goal, the Q-function of each individual agent will append a mixing term containing the average Q-function of neighboring agents received via communication networks. Simulation results demonstrate that the inclusion of this mixing term in each individual Q-function can indeed enhance the convergence speed for plug-and-play operations within isolated AC MGs.

articleTitle: Experiences and Lessons Learned from Load Modelling for and Applications to Taiwan Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: This paper presents the experiences and lessons we have learned from load modelling for and applications to Taiwan power systems. First, a concise description of load modelling process is briefed. The description contains introduction to load models, modelling methodologies and also parameters identifications. Second, applying modelled loads to Taiwan power systems analyses are examined. These analyses cover transient stability critical clearing time (CCT), small signal stability, and voltage stability. Finally, experiences and lessons learned from modelling loads for and applying to Taiwan power systems are summarised in eleven recommendations. It is our wish that these eleven recommendations can help power engineers and researchers to circumvent load modelling pitfalls.

articleTitle: A Novel QR-based Probabilistic Forecasting Method for Solar power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Solar power is quite intermittent in nature, where it is highly dependent on weather conditions. Therefore, accurate forecasting for solar power generation is essential. Probabilistic forecasts with an uncertainty analysis provide a more comprehensive forecast application. Previous research works have proposed numerous methods for probabilistic forecasts, such as quantile regression, interval, density forecasting, and etc. However, these methods still have many drawbacks. Thus, this paper aims to analyze and control the uncertainty of PV power forecasts, and conducts more in-depth researches on the forecasting methods. The main contribution of this paper is to propose a new probabilistic forecasting process, which can distinguish the data variation of power generation at PV sites and automatically select the optimal method to perform the forecasting. This method can not only obtain accurate results, but also potentially reduce the operation time significantly.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review on Roadmap to Seaports: Methodologies, Area of Use, and Purposes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The maritime sector is experiencing significant change, creating challenges and opportunities for seaports. This review explores the evolving landscape of seaports by analyzing various academic papers, providing a roadmap for understanding their changing nature. This paper examines the historical development of seaports, focusing on the latest fifth generation, emphasizing sustainability, intelligent services, and community engagement. The introduction of All-Electric Ships and the growing need for sustainability requires innovative strategies. This study suggests two solutions: two-stage robust voltage control and flexible management approaches. Through keyword analysis, the review identified three primary research themes: methodologies used in ports, their purpose, and the adoption of smart control technologies. Each theme is thoroughly explored in subsequent sections, offering a detailed examination based on papers sourced from IEEE Explore spanning the years 2000 to 2023.

articleTitle: Variable Architecture Multi-Island Microgrids for Industrial Plant Expansions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: Many industrial expansion projects aim to approach a new power system mantaining it separate from existing ones, instead this paper demonstrates how integrating existing and new power systems can enhance the reliability through the management of a power system with variable architecture. The paper suggests an innovative approach to be adopted for the power system expansion for industrial plants that require high level of service continuity, consisting in a variable architecture multi-island microgrid. The salient features of the suggested system and the main functions of the Electrical Power Management System (EPMS) are illustrated. EPMS strategies allow to activate a load shedding system operation. The operation and the results under different contingency are reported. The results highlight the increasing of the service continuity.

articleTitle: Stochastic Harmonics Evaluation for Offshore Wind Farms Grid Connection Impact Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE/IAS 60th Industrial and Commercial Power Systems Technical Conference (I&CPS)
abstract: The offshore wind power plant grid-connected harmonic analysis is inherently influenced by numerous uncertainties, which introduce a level of risk to the analysis results. To address this, stochastic analysis emerges as a viable approach for assessing such a problem. To provide more reliable analysis results, a stochastic harmonics evaluation approach is proposed in this paper for offshore wind farm grid connection impact study. The behaviors of critical parameters, such as active components that contribute harmonic currents and passive components that affect harmonic power flows, external grid background harmonics, and system topology, are modeled in a stochastic way and taken into account in harmonic power flow computation by Monte Carlo simulations. Test results of a real-world offshore wind farm grid connection impact study are presented and compared with those obtained by a deterministic method.
